messages.author: 4b76b20a5563270e
messages.subject: "Page Not Found" for some users but not all
parts:
Hi folks,

I'm past what I can easily diagnose because it's not an issue I can reproduce on my machines, so I could use some more tips for how to diagnose these problems, or perhaps they're known issues. 

The gist of it: I'm running a whole suite of Shiny apps that appear at war-on-ice.com, through a back-end server (vincerdata.com) and iframes. For most users, there is no problem. For two (who happen to be heavy users) there are issues where nothing at all loads.

Here are the issues I've been able to glean:

1) Sometimes the static elements in ui.R alone load -- not the elements cooked up in server.R and passed to ui.R, like

onload.seasongcode <- reactive (something here)
 output$onload.seasongcode <-
        renderUI (textInput (inputId="seasongcode", label="Game ID", value = onload.seasongcode()))

2) Sometimes nothing loads at all, and the Javascript pops up with this

so I asked one of my users to do this and try the diagnostics, and he said

"they're all returning 404 not found errors when it attempts to access the JSON or the bootstrap.css.map"

I fixed the bootstrap.css.map issue but that seems to be unrelated to the Shiny, since that's in the containing page.

3) For one of these users, the issue only just started yesterday. I don't think he changed anything along the way, so it might be a ports issue from his ISP. I should note that I have the shiny server running on port 80 already.

Any insight would be appreciated.

AT

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: "Page Not Found" for some users but not all
parts:
Okay, you were using shiny 0.9.1, four versions behind the latest one
(same thing for the R version). I'm not quite sure if you need to
upgrade R/R packages, since you use DataTables extensively, and
DataTables has been upgraded to 1.10.x
(http://blog.rstudio.org/2014/10/02/shiny-0-10-2/), which may or may
not break your tables, depending on how much you used custom
initialization options. You may try to upgrade R and R packages
locally, and see if all the tables still work well.

I believe the original problem was an R problem, even though it was
manifested in JS/HTML. There have been a few bug fixes since shiny
0.9.1, which might be relevant.

Regards,
Yihui
